vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: comic-script
Version: 2.2.0

The skill bundle is a straightforward utility for generating comic script templates and character sheets. The core logic in `scripts/comic.sh` consists of a Python script that formats text based on user input for storyboards and dialogue tips, with no evidence of network activity, file system access, or malicious intent.

llm.summary: The skill mostly does what its description says (generates comic/storyboard text), but there are small incoherences in documentation vs. implementation and the bundled script expects python3 even though no binaries are declared—these mismatches warrant review before installing.

dimensions.detail: The described purpose (comic storyboard, panels, dialogue, character sheets, layout) matches the behavior of the included scripts: they generate storyboard, character, dialogue, and layout text. However the SKILL.md command table lists commands (create, panel, expression, scene, pacing) that do not appear in the actual script (which implements storyboard, character, dialogue, layout). Also the package contains an executable script that invokes python3, but the registry metadata declares no required binaries—this is an uncovered runtime requirement.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md is instruction-only and does not tell the agent to read unrelated files, environment variables, or contact external endpoints. The included shell script runs an embedded Python program and prints static output; it does not perform file I/O, network access, or credential use. The mismatch between documented commands and implemented commands is a scope/documentation inconsistency that could confuse users or agents.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec; the skill is instruction-only with a bundled script. Nothing is downloaded from external URLs and no archives are extracted, so installation risk is low.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables, credentials, or config paths and the code does not read any. No secrets or unrelated credentials are requested.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and there are no privileges requested. The skill does not attempt to persist configuration or modify other skills. Autonomous invocation is allowed by default (normal) but not combined with other privilege concerns.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to generate comic/storyboard text and contains a small shell script that runs an embedded Python snippet. Before installing: (1) note the documentation mismatch — SKILL.md lists commands not present in the script; ask the author for corrected docs or an updated script. (2) the script invokes python3 but the metadata does not declare python3 as a required binary—ensure your environment has python3 available if you plan to run it. (3) because the source and homepage are unknown, review the included scripts yourself (scripts/comic.sh) in a safe environment to confirm there are no unexpected network calls or file operations. If you need greater assurance, request the author to declare runtime dependencies and fix the command documentation or run the skill in a sandboxed environment first.
